content.value_statement: Hybrid Next.js and Docusaurus deployments can require ordered build steps and precise hosting settings. This skill explains the documented build flow and required Vercel environment variables.
actual_capabilities: Explains the documented order for building Docusaurus documentation and a Next.js application.
Identifies the output directory used for generated documentation.
Describes the referenced Vercel configuration file and FastAPI runtime.
Notes that API routes are rewritten to the Python function.
Lists the environment-variable names required in the Vercel Dashboard.
limitations: Does not run builds, deploy applications, or change Vercel settings.
Does not validate package dependencies, build scripts, or deployment results.
Does not provide secret values or manage credentials.
Assumes the referenced project structure and configuration files exist.

use_cases.title: Prepare a first Vercel deployment
use_cases.description: Review the documented build order and required settings before deploying a hybrid application.

use_cases.title: Hand off deployment knowledge
use_cases.description: Share a concise deployment reference with a teammate who maintains documentation and application builds.

use_cases.title: Check environment setup
use_cases.description: Compare Vercel Dashboard variable names with the documented deployment requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: explain the build
prompt_templates.scenario: You are new to the project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the documented hybrid build process in numbered steps. Use simple language.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: prepare deployment
prompt_templates.scenario: You are preparing a Vercel release.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a pre-deployment checklist from this skill. Include the build order, configuration, and environment-variable names.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: troubleshoot configuration
prompt_templates.scenario: You need to review a deployment setup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my described Vercel setup with this skill. Identify missing documented configuration or environment-variable names. Do not request secret values.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: create handoff notes
prompt_templates.scenario: You are documenting an operational handoff.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft concise deployment handoff notes based only on this skill. Separate build steps, routing details, and environment-variable names.

output: Copy generated documentation into that directory.

output_examples.input: What must be configured before deployment?
output: Set the listed environment-variable names in the Vercel Dashboard.

best_practices: Confirm that the project structure matches the documented paths before running a build.
Store secret values only in the Vercel Dashboard or another approved secret manager.
Test the build and deployment in a controlled environment before production release.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys or authentication secrets into prompts, source files, or logs.
Do not assume the documented commands validate dependencies or deployment health.
Do not change routing rules without reviewing the referenced Vercel configuration.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy my application?
faq.answer: No. It documents the deployment pipeline and settings.

faq.question: Does this skill run build commands?
faq.answer: No. It explains the documented commands but does not execute them.

faq.question: Which hosting platform does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers the documented Vercel deployment configuration.

faq.question: Which application types are described?
faq.answer: It describes a Next.js application, Docusaurus documentation, and a FastAPI backend.

faq.question: Does it provide secret values?
faq.answer: No. It lists required variable names and never provides secret values.

faq.question: Can it verify a successful deployment?
faq.answer: No. You must run your own build, deployment, and validation checks.
